sections.heading: 1. Key Expressions & Sentences Reviewed (Lessons 8–14)
points: Lesson 8: "Dzoka kumusha nekukurumidza kana wapedza basa." — Return home quickly when you finish work.
Lesson 9: "Makorokoto, wabudirira!" — Congratulations, you have succeeded!
Lesson 10: "Tora kapu iyi uiise pedyo nefafitera usati wabuda." — Take this cup and put it near the window before you go out.
Lesson 11: "Ndinonzwa nzara mangwanani kana ndisina kudya." — I feel hungry in the morning if I have not eaten.
Lesson 12: "Chigara pano womirira kusvika ndadzoka kubva kuchechi." — Sit right here and wait until I return from church.
Lesson 13: "Uyai kuno mundibatsire kusimudza zvinhu zvinorema izvi." — Come here and help me lift these heavy things.
Lesson 14: "Vhara musuwo zvinyoronyoro nokuti mwana achiri akarara." — Close the door gently because the baby is still asleep.

sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Giving Commands & Polite Requests ('Dzoka'): Singular Command: Verb stem (-a) [Huya! / Tora!] | Polite or Plural Command: Verb stem + -i (-ai) [Huyai! / Torai!]
Celebrating Milestones with 'Makorokoto!': Makorokoto + ne- + ku-[verb] = Congratulations on [doing something]! (e.g., Makorokoto nekubudirira!)
Giving Commands & Polite Requests ('Tora'): Singular Command: Verb stem (-a) [Huya! / Tora!] | Polite or Plural Command: Verb stem + -i (-ai) [Huyai! / Torai!]
Shona Greetings & Time of Day ('mangwanani'): Morning: Mangwanani | Afternoon: Masikati | Evening: Manheru | How are you?: Makadini? / Wakadii?
Giving Commands & Polite Requests ('Chigara'): Singular Command: Verb stem (-a) [Huya! / Tora!] | Polite or Plural Command: Verb stem + -i (-ai) [Huyai! / Torai!]
Giving Commands & Polite Requests ('Uyai'): Singular Command: Verb stem (-a) [Huya! / Tora!] | Polite or Plural Command: Verb stem + -i (-ai) [Huyai! / Torai!]

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: The Rural Homestead ('Kumusha') & Urban–Rural Family Ties: The word 'musha' (locative 'kumusha') means both 'home' and the ancestral rural homestead.

Peer Encouragement & Celebrating Personal Achievements: While 'Makorokoto nekubudirira kwenyu' uses the respectful plural 'kwenyu', saying 'Makorokoto, wabudirira!' uses the warm singular prefix 'wa-' ('you have succeeded') used between close friends, classmates, or by a parent praising a child who has just passed a test or mastered a new skill..

Kitchen Orderliness & Borrowed Household Words ('Fafitera' vs 'Hwindo'): Notice the word 'fafitera' ('window') alongside 'kapu' ('cup')! Shona has enriched its everyday household vocabulary over the past century by adapting words from both Afrikaans ('venster' -> 'fafitera', 'tafel' -> 'tafura') and English ('window' -> 'hwindo', 'cup' -> 'kapu'), all seamlessly fitted into Shona syllable structure where every word ends in a vowel..
Traditional & Modern Zimbabwean Breakfasts ('Chikafu cheMangwanani'): A hearty morning meal is essential before starting school or farm work.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 2 — Food & Shopping: How do you say 'I bought bread and milk at the shop' in Shona?
review_exercises.explanation: 'Ndakatenga' = 'I bought', 'chingwa nemukaka' = 'bread and milk', 'kuchitoro' = 'at the shop'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 2 — Colours & Questions: Complete the question: '______ hembe yaunoda kupfeka, chena kana tsvuku?' (Which shirt do you want to wear, the white one or the red one?)
review_exercises.explanation: 'Ndeipi' asks 'Which one?' for nouns like 'mota' (car) or 'hembe' (shirt).

review_exercises.prompt: Review 2 — Talking About Time: If someone says 'Chimirira kwemaminitsi mashanu chete', how long are they asking you to wait?
options: Until the end of the month

review_exercises.prompt: Review 2 — Future Plans ('-cha-'): Which verb correctly completes 'Mangwana ______ sadza nenyama' ('Tomorrow we will cook sadza and meat')?
Review 2 — Negative Present: In 'Ndiri kutsvaga makiyi angu asi handisi kuawona', what does 'handisi kuawona' mean?
options: I left them in the car
I found them on the table
I will buy new ones tomorrow
review_exercises.explanation: 'Handisi' ('I am not') + 'ku-a-wona' ('seeing them [the keys]') means 'I do not see them'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 2 — Translate this new review sentence: 'Wedzera shuga shoma mukapu yetii.'
options: Put the warm water on the table please.
We bought maize meal and cooking oil yesterday.
I feel hungry when I wake up early.
Add a little sugar into the cup of tea.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Add a little sugar into the cup of tea.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Wedzera' = 'Add', 'shuga shoma' = 'a little sugar', 'mukapu yetii' = 'into the cup of tea'.
